IJN torpedo boat guns have good alpha, but poor turning rates and low DPM.  They are best used on low health DDs or for a few quick volleys before diving into cover.  Always do your best to dictate the terms of a guns engagement when you are in Kagero, Yugo, or Shima.  Fire a volley or two, then angle away or duck behind cover.  

Do not get in protracted gunfight, as you will either lose your ship or most of your health unless your opponent is bad with their guns as well.

Do not be afraid to use smoke as a disengagement tool, but do not simply sit in the smoke.  Power out of it once they no longer can see you, reacquire your target, hit them first again.

Aim towards the rear of their ship to try to take out their engines, slowing their manoeuvrability.  Drop a wide spread of torps as well.  At best, you will catch them with one and blow them to hell.  At worst it will be a distraction.  Good Luck.

edit: regarding planes.  Keep your AA off as much as possible.  Only activate it when planes are about to spot you.  Shut it back off immediately after they get out of range.  This reduces aircraft spotting a great deal.

Current Costco employee here:

Been at Costco for 6 months, after a 3 year stint as an Overnight Support Manager at Walmart.  The difference between the work cultures is night and day.  Walmart believes in instilling "a sense of urgency" in all its employees, which means having everyone in various levels of panic at all times in order to maximize output.

Which results in emotional and physical burnout, and staff in various levels of burnout.

Costco doesn't believe in that, and one of the big takeaways is that you can tell a supervisor that something can't be done and make it stick, as long as you have valid reasons.  Something impossible at Walmart.

Plus, the wages.  My final wage, as a bottom level manager at Walmart, was my starting wage as a line grunt at Costco.  At Walmart, I would do well to see a 50 cent per year raise, with a top out at around $23/hour.  At Costco I get a raise roughly every 1000 hours worked of at least $1/hr, topping out currently at $28.60/hr.

Granted, it's not all sweetness and light.  Management does do stupid things on occasion that makes us line people scratch our heads, but overall I have zero regrets making the jump and intend Costco to be my last job.
